narrative: Markets are navigating the aftermath of US midterm elections, where a Democratic sweep is expected to result in government gridlock and policy restraint. While the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 initially rallied as election uncertainty eased, a sharp rotation is underway out of tech and semiconductors into the consumer sector. This shift is fueled by disappointing guidance from chipmakers and growing skepticism regarding the sustainability of AI infrastructure returns. Concurrently, oil prices have collapsed on optimism for a resolution to the Iran conflict, while gold has surged to record levels above $4,000.

Nasdaq.why: Winnie Hsu notes a bearish rotation out of tech as investors re-evaluate the AI narrative, though anchors highlight a rally as election uncertainty dissipated.

S&P 500.why: Anchors report the index rallied as election uncertainty eased, with the equal-weighted version reaching an all-time high.

Gold.why: Stephen Carroll notes prices moved back above the $4,000 psychological level amid broader market uncertainty.

Oil.why: Oliver Crook reports prices fell nearly 10% on expectations of a potential end to the Iran war and general demand concerns.

priced_in: A Bank of England rate hike
Easing of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East
Potential for a more restrictive regulatory environment and data center moratoriums
A more muted election reaction compared to previous cycles
debates: Sustainability of AI revenue growth versus current capacity constraints
Whether government gridlock will successfully restrain massive tax and spending bills
The impact of a Democratic sweep on future fiscal deficits
watch_next: Bank of England interest rate decision
